newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends sharply up as funds buy, meal up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends sharply up as funds buy, meal up.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended sharply higher on aggressive fund buying tied to technical indicators and soymeal also ended firmer as soybeans rallied, pit sources said.

Funds bought at least 4,500 lots of soyoil on the day after weather-related strength helped the December plow through the 40-day moving average. Traders said the next target area in the December was the 50-day moving average which stood at 23.25 cents a lb.
Weather was the catalyst, driving soybeans to double- digit gains and providing strength to soy products.

Forecasts called for mild temperatures this week, followed by a warmer weekend with no significant moisture expected in Illinois until at least August 6. Hot, dry weather can stress soybean crops during blooming.

USDA on Monday said 68 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was blooming. USDA also said 62 percent of the crop was rated good to excellent, unchanged from the previous week. The market had been looking for an improvement.
Soymeal ended $7.00 to $1.30 per ton higher with December up $7.00 at $209.20 a ton. Soyoil closed 0.75 to 0.62 cent per lb higher with December up 0.71 at 22.86 cents.

Traders also pointed to escalating concerns about dry weather in portions of China's grain/soy belt. The most severe drought in more than four decades has hit China's northern province of Hebei, affecting more than half the region's farmland.

Gains in the August soymeal were held back by slack meal demand, said Bill Biedermann, director of research for Allendale Inc. Biedermann said Illinois processors were having trouble moving soymeal at $18 over CBOT August.

On the day, funds bought at least 4,500 lots of soyoil, led by Griffin Trading. Griffin bought 500 lots each August and December, Rosenthal Collins and Prudential Securities each bought 800 December and Smith Barney bought 500 December and 200 August, traders said.
Produce Grain bought 500 each September and October and 300 December while ADM, Cargill and Central Soya were all said to be sellers, floor sources said.
In soymeal, Smith Barney bought 400 December and 200 each August and September while Produce Grain bought 200 September and 300 August, traders said. Tenco Inc sold 800 August.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 26,000 lots, against Monday's 21,235.
Soyoil volume was pegged at 35,000 lots, against Monday's 19,161.
